# Damage-curve catalogue

<!-- Generated by scripts/reference_helpers/build_damage_curve_catalogue.py from docs/cells/catalogue/*.json. Do not edit by hand; edit the entry and rebuild. -->

Every damage curve in this repository, by asset and hazard: 13 live cells, 5 proposals, 3 reused bindings and 4 gaps. Older versions that a newer one replaced are left out. Each entry was drafted by an agent from the cell's own files and has not yet been read by the cell owner or the reviewer.

## How to read this catalogue

**Status.**

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Live | In the runtime artifact index (`docs/contracts/machine_readable_artifact_index.json`); the platform can call it |
| Proposal | Built and validated in the repository but not in the runtime index; waiting for review |
| Reused | No curve of its own; a consumer binding prices this asset with another cell's curve |
| Gap | No curve yet |

**Evidence tiers.** Each curve gets two tiers from the cell's own tier table. *Shape* is the evidence for how damage rises with the hazard. *Cost* is the evidence for turning that damage into a share of value. When one source gives damage directly as a share of value (for example a FEMA Hazus loss ratio), shape and cost share that tier. Lower is stronger.

| Tier | Repository label | Plain meaning |
|---|---|---|
| T1 · Claims or field calibrated | `T1_claims_or_field_calibrated` | Fitted to insurance claims or field damage surveys of the same kind of asset. |
| T2 · Public lab, standard or physics | `T2_public_lab_standard_or_physics` | Taken from a published standard, a public model such as FEMA Hazus, lab tests or physics. |
| T3 · Engineering proxy or adjacent evidence | `T3_engineering_proxy_or_adjacent_empirical` | Borrowed from a similar asset or a related study, with an engineering step to make it fit. |
| T4 · Placeholder or expert judgment | `T4_placeholder_or_expert_judgment` | Our own judgment where no source gives the number; visible, never a silent default. |

**Scope words.** *Not covered* lists parts that are inside the asset's value but have no curve, so the loss for them is missing. *Out of scope* lists things outside the asset's value or priced by another cell. *Missing mechanisms* are kinds of damage that a covered part's curve leaves out.

**Notes on a curve row** (at most two): *Reused from* · *Not a Hazard profile* · *Opt-in only* · *Key assumption* · *Known bias*. *Opt-in only* means the platform must pass an explicit acknowledgement code before the curve answers.

**Checks.** A *curve check* compares the curve itself with outside data in this repository. A *result check* compares the finished loss with outside loss numbers in the Hazard repository (`docs/data_sources/financial_range_*`).

## Cells

<a id="hail-solar"></a>

### Solar farm × Hail

**Live** · model v1.0, docs r7 · `hail_solar` · [curve file](hail_solar/current/hail_solar__model_v1_0__docs_r7__curve_artifact.json) · 2026-10-19: Agent-drafted, from the cell's own tier table, value profiles and capability declaration

**Input:** MESH-equivalent maximum hail diameter (mm; inches are converted), 0 to 100 mm (clamp or warn)

**Method:** Fitted to data. Logistic curves per module type fitted to public PVEL/Kiwa hail-test breakage anchors and the IEC baseline; glass-breakage probability used as the module replacement ratio.

| Part | Curves | Variants | Shape | Cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PV modules (glass and cells) | `HAIL_SOLAR_FRAGILE_THIN_GG`<br>`HAIL_SOLAR_DEFAULT_3P2_GBS`<br>`HAIL_SOLAR_HARDENED_THICKER` | module type: fragile thin glass-glass / default 3.2 mm glass-backsheet / hail-hardened thicker glass; optional tracker stow blend | T2 · D50 and slope fitted to public lab anchors (fragile and default T2; hardened variant T3) | T2 · Direct module-hardware value share from the NLR Q1-2025 basis (T2); optional Hazard-adapter profile is T4 | *Key assumption:* Glass-breakage probability is used as the module replacement ratio<br>*Opt-in only:* Stow adjustment applies only when a stow state is supplied (T4 placeholder) |

**How to use this curve**

- Damage is a share of: Replacement value of the PV modules; the plant share comes from a named value profile (direct module hardware, or the Hazard-compatible adapter) or a site value basis, with no default
- Single event: allowed: module damage ratio (missing module type uses the default curve with a flag)
- Scenario dollars: conditional: needs a named value profile or site value basis and an exposure fraction
- Yearly loss: conditional: computed by the consumer from a frequency-driven loss simulation with caps applied and known-answer tests passing; curve spread not carried
- Condition: Exactly one module type must match; a missing type uses the default with DEFAULT_SELECTOR_USED, an unknown type is rejected
- Condition: Hail size unit must be stated; inches are converted to mm
- Condition: Stow probability is the event-time stow state, not hail frequency; stow results carry the placeholder flag
- Condition: A value profile must be named; none is applied implicitly

**Scope**

- Not covered: Racking structure (secondary, open; no curve); Tracker steel (used only as a stow conditioner; direct damage has no curve); SCADA and met instruments (optional secondary; no curve); Inverters, substation, foundations, civil works and drainage (treated as no direct hail damage by coverage decision; no curve)
- Out of scope: Yearly and tail loss metrics (computed by the consumer, not the cell); Site value and exposure basis (supplied by the consumer)
- Missing mechanisms: Cell cracking or latent performance loss without glass breakage; Wind-driven hail hitting the module face (open seam, not in the diameter-only curve)

**Key sources** (taken from the cell's write-up)

- PVEL, 2023 Hail Stress Sequence results (PVEL_2023_HSS)
- Kiwa PVEL, Hail Stress Sequence scorecard (KIWA_PVEL_HSS)
- IEC 61215 hail test baseline (IEC_61215_BASELINE)
- VDE Americas, hail-stow technical memo (E_VDE_HAIL_STOW)
- DOE/FEMP, Hail Damage Mitigation for Solar PV Systems (DOE_FEMP_HAIL_GUIDANCE)

**Our judgment (T4 items)**

- Tracker stow shifts the curve by +8 mm (direction supported, size not calibrated)
- Stowed modules capped at 90% damage
- Hazard-compatible value profile assigns all general replacement fieldwork to the modules

**Outside checks**

- Result check, Hazard repo: Financial range check (Hazard repo): industry loss figures for solar hail ([link](https://github.com/aamani-ai/Hazard_Modeling/blob/main/docs/data_sources/financial_range_solar_hail/profile.md))

**Open items**

- Recalibrate if claims show replacement policy differs from glass-breakage probability
- Wind-driven hail contact effect needs event wind and tracker orientation data
- Stow adjustment awaits tracker stow-angle impact testing
- Notebook walkthrough source paths are not repository-current

**Files:** [write-up](hail_solar/current/hail_solar_curve_derivation_dossier_v1_3.md) · [notebooks](../../notebooks/hail/solar)

<a id="flood-solar"></a>

### Solar farm × Flood

**Live** · model v1.0, docs r4 · `flood_solar` · [curve file](flood_solar/current/flood_solar__model_v1_0__docs_r4__curve_artifact.json) · 2026-10-19: Agent-drafted, from the cell's own tier table and capability declaration

**Input:** Water surface elevation or site flood depth (m), turned into local depth above each part's critical elevation, 0 to 2 m (clamp or warn); foundations use flow velocity (m/s) or a scour proxy, 0 to 4

**Method:** Built from references. Piecewise depth-damage points per part, set by engineering judgment from DOE/FEMP solar flood guidance and NEMA water-damaged equipment guidance, in the USACE depth-percent table form.

| Part | Curves | Variants | Shape | Cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Inverters | `FS_INV` | none (enclosure rating is recorded as a flag; no alternate curve) | T3 · Engineering depth-damage points; mechanism from DOE/FEMP and NEMA | T3 · Points already give damage as a share of the part's replacement value (same table) |  |
| Switchgear | `FS_SWG` | none (enclosure rating is recorded as a flag; no alternate curve) | T3 · Engineering depth-damage points; mechanism from DOE/FEMP and NEMA | T3 · Points already give damage as a share of the part's replacement value (same table) |  |
| Main transformer and controls | `FS_XFMR` | none (transformer type is a flag and a future variant) | T3 · Engineering depth-damage points; mechanism from DOE/FEMP and NEMA | T3 · Points already give damage as a share of the part's replacement value (same table) | *Key assumption:* Rises more slowly than other cabinets because a liquid-filled transformer may be reconditioned |
| Combiner boxes and DC protection | `FS_COMB` | none | T3 · Engineering depth-damage points; mechanism from DOE/FEMP and NEMA | T3 · Points already give damage as a share of the part's replacement value (same table) |  |
| SCADA and monitoring cabinets | `FS_SCADA` | none | T3 · Engineering depth-damage points; mechanism from DOE/FEMP and NEMA | T3 · Points already give damage as a share of the part's replacement value (same table) |  |
| AC and DC collection cable | `FS_CABLE` | none (cable wet-location rating is a future variant) | T3 · Engineering points for wet terminations and conduit contamination | T3 · Points already give damage as a share of the part's replacement value (same table) | *Key assumption:* Pathway and termination exposure axis; its unit and formula are not fully pinned |
| PV modules | `FS_PVMOD` | none | T3 · Engineering submersion points | T3 · Points already give damage as a share of the part's replacement value (same table) | *Key assumption:* Applies only when water reaches the module's lower edge |
| Foundations | `FS_FOUND` | none | T4 · Generic velocity/scour placeholder points | T4 · Points already give damage as a share of the part's replacement value (same T4 table) | *Key assumption:* Placeholder; replace with a site hydraulic or geotechnical assessment where material |

**How to use this curve**

- Damage is a share of: Replacement value of the same part (its own value bucket), never total project value
- Single event: allowed: per-part damage ratio
- Scenario dollars: conditional: needs an explicit part value and exposure fraction (fraction_value_exposed)
- Yearly loss: conditional: computed by the consumer from a frequency-driven loss simulation with caps applied; curve spread not carried
- Condition: Equipment elevations must use the same vertical datum as the water surface; unknown or incompatible datum fails closed
- Condition: Local depth above 2 m clamps or warns
- Condition: Flow velocity is required to evaluate the foundation curve
- Condition: Do not apply a part's damage ratio to total project value or count shared support cost twice

**Scope**

- Not covered: Mounting and racking structure (debris and velocity load is a candidate mechanism; no curve); Civil works: roads, access and fencing (reviewed in the write-up; no curve); Site drainage and flood defences (treated as protection state, not a damaged part)
- Out of scope: Yearly and tail loss metrics (computed by the consumer, not the cell); Part values and exposure fractions (supplied by the consumer; not embedded in the curve file)
- Missing mechanisms: Flood duration, salinity and contamination (flags only, no numeric effect); Energised versus shut-down state at flooding (flag only); Water reaching equipment through conduits when the cabinet itself is above water (flag only, no multiplier); Debris impact on modules

**Key sources** (taken from the cell's write-up)

- DOE/FEMP, Preventing and Mitigating Flood Damage to Solar PV Systems (DOE_FEMP_PV_FLOOD)
- NEMA GD 1-2019, Evaluating Water-Damaged Electrical Equipment (NEMA_GD1_2019)
- NEMA, Enclosure Types (NEMA_ENCLOSURE_TYPES)
- FEMA P-348, Protecting Building Utility Systems from Flood Damage (FEMA_P348)
- USACE HEC-FIA, Depth-Percent Damage Relationships (USACE_HEC_FIA)

**Our judgment (T4 items)**

- Foundation scour curve is a generic placeholder; site hydraulics and geotechnics decide real damage

**Outside checks**

- Result check, Hazard repo: Financial range check (Hazard repo): industry loss figures for solar flood ([link](https://github.com/aamani-ai/Hazard_Modeling/blob/main/docs/data_sources/financial_range_solar_flood/profile.md))

**Open items**

- No claims, OEM or forensic calibration; damage points are engineering parameterisation
- Transformer type, flood duration and salinity are open seams (candidate model v1.1 items)
- Cable pathway axis unit and formula are not fully pinned in the curve file
- Surveyed equipment elevations and conduit routing are needed per site

**Files:** [write-up](flood_solar/current/flood_solar_curve_derivation_dossier_v1_0.md) · [notebooks](../../notebooks/flood/solar)

<a id="tropical-cyclone-wind-solar"></a>

### Solar farm × Hurricane wind

**Live** · model v2.1, docs r2 · `tropical_cyclone_wind_solar` · [curve file](tropical_cyclone_wind_solar/current/tropical_cyclone_wind_solar__model_v2_1__docs_r2__curve_artifact.json) · 2026-10-19: Agent-drafted, from the cell's own tier table, source register and decision log

**Input:** Demand ratio 0 to 2, withheld above 2: arrays use event/design net pressure (fixed tilt) or tracker-normal gust / exact-system critical gust (tracker); site facilities use event/design wind pressure or a gust-squared proxy. The satellite-data module route uses event maximum gust, 17.4 to 39.1 m/s

**Method:** Built from references. Ordered damage-state curves with Tier-4 synthetic resistance medians and cost ratios (cell-local decision, no direct TC calibration source); one module route fitted to NREL satellite storm-damage records.

| Part | Curves | Variants | Shape | Cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PV module field | `TCWS2_FIXED_MODULE_SYNTHETIC_T4_ORDERED_STATES`<br>`TCWS2_TRACKER_MODULE_SYNTHETIC_T4_ORDERED_STATES` | architecture: fixed tilt / qualified single-axis tracker; resistance scenario: lower / central (headline) / upper | T4 · Synthetic resistance medians and spread | T4 · Synthetic damage-state cost ratios |  |
| PV module hardware, satellite-data route | `TCWS_PERRY_GROUND_FIXED_VISIBLE_REPLACEMENT_PROXY_V1` | none (ground-mounted fixed sites only) | T3 · Monotone fit to 34 satellite-labelled site records (source data T1, fit T3) | T4 · Uniform module value and full replacement of visible damage assumed | *Opt-in only:* Source-compatible sites only; cannot be combined with the generic fixed-tilt module curve |
| Mounting structure | `TCWS2_FIXED_STRUCTURE_SYNTHETIC_T4_ORDERED_STATES`<br>`TCWS2_TRACKER_SBOS_SYNTHETIC_T4_ORDERED_STATES` | architecture: fixed-tilt support structure / tracker structural BOS; resistance scenario: lower / central (headline) / upper | T4 · Synthetic resistance medians and spread | T4 · Synthetic damage-state cost ratios |  |
| Foundations | `TCWS21_FOUNDATION_SCREENING_T4_ORDERED_STATES` | resistance scenario: lower / central (headline) / upper | T4 · Synthetic resistance medians and spread | T4 · Synthetic damage-state cost ratios | *Key assumption:* Uses the site-facility demand ratio, not the array ratio |
| Power conversion and collection | `TCWS21_POWER_COLLECTION_SCREENING_T4_ORDERED_STATES` | resistance scenario: lower / central (headline) / upper | T4 · Synthetic resistance medians and spread | T4 · Synthetic damage-state cost ratios | *Key assumption:* Uses the site-facility demand ratio, not the array ratio |
| GSU and substation | `TCWS21_GSU_SUBSTATION_SCREENING_T4_ORDERED_STATES` | resistance scenario: lower / central (headline) / upper | T4 · Synthetic resistance medians and spread | T4 · Synthetic damage-state cost ratios | *Key assumption:* Uses the site-facility demand ratio, not the array ratio |
| SCADA and communications | `TCWS21_SCADA_SCREENING_T4_ORDERED_STATES` | resistance scenario: lower / central (headline) / upper | T4 · Synthetic resistance medians and spread | T4 · Synthetic damage-state cost ratios | *Key assumption:* Uses the site-facility demand ratio, not the array ratio |
| Civil infrastructure | `TCWS21_CIVIL_SCREENING_T4_ORDERED_STATES` | resistance scenario: lower / central (headline) / upper | T4 · Synthetic resistance medians and spread | T4 · Synthetic damage-state cost ratios | *Key assumption:* Uses the site-facility demand ratio, not the array ratio |

**How to use this curve**

- Damage is a share of: Replacement value of the same part; the plant view uses the named 2024-USD physical replacement profile, which must be requested and is never selected silently
- Single event: conditional: needs the qualified architecture-specific demand input; trackers need exact-system qualification and attained stow state
- Scenario dollars: conditional: needs the named value profile, a representative array exposure basis and a positive capacity_kwdc
- Yearly loss: conditional: computed by the consumer after exact pin, frequency-intensity coupling, cap and value validation, and an explicit decision to accept screening grade
- Condition: Array architecture is required and has no default; architectures are mutually exclusive
- Condition: Commanded stow is not enough; trackers must prove attained state
- Condition: Rain, debris, surge and tornado are excluded from this wind-only ratio and acknowledged separately
- Condition: Unbridged 10 m gust, storm category or NHC sustained wind is rejected as input

**Scope**

- Not covered: Replacement support (inspection, labour, rental, logistics, removal): no own curve; takes the value-weighted damage ratio of the other parts and is counted once
- Out of scope: Storm surge, flood, tornado and straight-line convective wind (separate pathways or cells); Hail, lightning and fire; Downtime, business interruption and insurance terms; Soft, sunk and non-physical cost (installed capex above physical replacement value)
- Missing mechanisms: Windborne debris impact as a separately valued pathway; Wind-driven rain and water ingress

**Key sources** (from the cell's source register)

- NREL/NLR, Satellite Imagery of PV Site Storm Damage dataset, 2025 (TCWS-S020)
- NREL, Q1-2025 Solar PV System Cost Benchmarks (TCWS-S013)
- DOE/FEMP, Toward Solar PV Storm Resilience field investigation (TCWS-S004)
- ASCE/SEI 7-22, Minimum Design Loads (TCWS-S005)
- Cell owner decision on synthetic Tier-4 parameters (TCWS2_CELL_LOCAL_SYNTHETIC_DECISION)

**Our judgment (T4 items)**

- Resistance medians and spreads for every array and facility curve are synthetic screening values
- Damage-state cost ratios for every part are synthetic
- The 0 to 2 demand range is a bounded synthetic domain; values above 2 are withheld
- Satellite-data route assumes uniform module value and full replacement of every visibly damaged module
- One representative array-zone curve is applied to the full array value

**Outside checks**

- Result check, Hazard repo: Financial range check (Hazard repo): industry loss figures for solar hurricane ([link](https://github.com/aamani-ai/Hazard_Modeling/blob/main/docs/data_sources/financial_range_solar_hurricane/profile.md))

**Open items**

- Tier-4 curves to be replaced by better evidence in a later model version
- Wind-field, direction-history and duration-cycling bridge contracts are named but their external content is unresolved
- Capability field status_before_promotion should become a clearer consumer-readiness field

<a id="strong-wind-solar"></a>

### Solar farm × Convective wind

**Live** · model v1.0, docs r3 · `strong_wind_solar` · [curve file](strong_wind_solar/current/strong_wind_solar__model_v1_0__docs_r3__curve_artifact.json) · 2026-10-19: Agent-drafted, from the cell's own tier table and capability declaration

**Next version:** Proposed model v2.0 (docs r1): straight-line convective wind only, separate fixed-tilt and qualified single-axis-tracker records with architecture-specific demand axes, bounded cascade, explicit value linkage and known-answer tests; T4 screening proxy, not canonical

**Input:** 3-second gust at array height (mph), 0 to 200 (warn or clamp), turned into a demand ratio: (gust / design gust) squared times stow and zone multipliers

**Method:** Built from references. Thresholded logistic curves on a design-normalised demand ratio; axis from wind-pressure physics, all numeric parameters set by engineering judgment from PV wind-load and storm-resilience sources.

| Part | Curves | Variants | Shape | Cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tracker structure | `SWS_TRACKER_STRUCT` | stow state: stowed / unstowed / probability blend; edge-zone multiplier | T4 · Threshold, midpoint and slope are engineering fits | T4 · 80% cap and 8% default value share, both T4 |  |
| Racking structure | `SWS_RACKING_STRUCT` | stow state: stowed / unstowed / probability blend; edge-zone multiplier | T4 · Threshold, midpoint and slope are engineering fits | T4 · 75% cap and 6% default value share, both T4 |  |
| PV module attachment | `SWS_MODULE_ATTACH` | stow state: stowed / unstowed / probability blend; edge-zone multiplier | T4 · Threshold, midpoint and slope are engineering fits | T4 · 65% cap and 40% default value share, both T4 | *Known bias:* No cascade rule with racking or tracker failure; summing can over-count |
| Foundations (uplift) | `SWS_FOUNDATION_UPLIFT` | none (foundation type is a future variant) | T4 · Threshold, midpoint and slope are engineering fits | T4 · 45% cap and 8% default value share, both T4 | *Key assumption:* Generic placeholder; pile and soil design are not modelled |
| Exposed SCADA and met station | `SWS_SCADA_EXPOSED` | none | T4 · Threshold, midpoint and slope are engineering fits | T4 · 15% cap and 2% default value share, both T4 |  |

**How to use this curve**

- Damage is a share of: Replacement value of the same part, as a share of the physical replaceable base (default shares are illustrative)
- Single event: allowed: per-part damage ratio
- Scenario dollars: conditional: needs an explicit value and exposure basis
- Yearly loss: conditional: computed by the consumer from a frequency-driven loss simulation with caps applied; curve spread not carried
- Condition: design_gust_mph and mounting_type are required
- Condition: Compute the demand ratio once; do not apply zone or terrain multipliers twice
- Condition: Multiply each damage ratio only by the same part's non-overlapping value
- Condition: Tornado and debris damage are not in this aerodynamic curve

**Scope**

- Not covered: The other 36% of the reference physical base (parts not named by the cell) has no curve or value share; the cell says this is not an automatic zero
- Out of scope: Tornado and windborne debris (deferred to a separate pathway); Yearly and tail loss metrics (computed by the consumer, not the cell)
- Missing mechanisms: Cascade between racking or tracker failure and module detachment (no dependency rule)

**Key sources** (taken from the cell's write-up)

- Wind-pressure physics, pressure scales with speed squared (WIND_PRESSURE_PHYSICS)
- CPP, utility-scale PV wind-load paper (CPP_PV_WIND_LOAD)
- CPP, torsional instability of single-axis trackers (CPP_TORSIONAL_TRACKER)
- DOE/FEMP, severe-weather PV design guidance (DOE_FEMP_SEVERE_WEATHER_PV)
- NREL, storm-resilience and storm-hardening reports (NREL_STORM_RESILIENCE)

**Our judgment (T4 items)**

- Damage thresholds, midpoints and slopes for every part are engineering fits
- Damage caps per part (15% to 80%) are engineering fits, not claims-calibrated
- Default part value shares are illustrative
- Stow multiplies demand by 0.80 (stowed) or 1.25 (unstowed or failed)

**Outside checks**

- None yet

**Open items**

- Workbook stow selector defect: Dashboard!G7 reads B7 instead of B8 (not patched in v1)
- No cell-specific known-answer test fixture for v1
- No claims or forensic calibration; v2.0 promotion is blocked pending independent review and stronger calibration

<a id="wildfire-solar"></a>

### Solar farm × Wildfire

**Live** · model v1.0, docs r3 · `wildfire_solar` · [curve file](wildfire_solar/current/wildfire_solar__model_v1_0__docs_r3__curve_artifact.json) · 2026-10-19: Agent-drafted, from the cell's own tier table, source registers and capability declaration

**Input:** USFS FSim conditional flame-length class, exact integer 1 to 6 (0 = no event), or the six-class probability vector; no interpolation; burn probability stays with Hazard

**Method:** Built from references. Exact-class state tables per part on FSim flame-length classes; ordering constrained by field, lab and guidance sources, absolute values set by engineering judgment.

| Part | Curves | Variants | Shape | Cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PV modules | `WSV1_MODULE_THERMAL` | none (only the central screening table exists) | T4 · Class values are engineering judgment | T2 · Reference part value from the NREL/NLR Q1-2025 benchmark crosswalk |  |
| Tracker and racking | `WSV1_RACKING_THERMAL` | none | T4 · Class values are engineering judgment | T2 · Reference part value from the NREL/NLR Q1-2025 benchmark crosswalk |  |
| Piles and inverter pads | `WSV1_FOUNDATION_THERMAL` | none | T4 · Class values are engineering judgment | T2 · Reference part value from the NREL/NLR Q1-2025 benchmark crosswalk | *Key assumption:* Low response for steel and concrete, not immunity |
| Central inverters | `WSV1_INVERTER_THERMAL` | none | T4 · Class values are engineering judgment | T2 · Reference part value from the NREL/NLR Q1-2025 benchmark crosswalk |  |
| Combiner boxes | `WSV1_COMBINER_THERMAL` | none | T4 · Class values are engineering judgment | T2 · Reference part value from the NREL/NLR Q1-2025 benchmark crosswalk |  |
| Exposed AC and DC cable | `WSV1_CABLE_EXPOSED` | none | T4 · Class values are engineering judgment | T2 · Reference part value from the NREL/NLR Q1-2025 benchmark crosswalk | *Known bias:* Reference profile counts all cable as exposed; buried or conduit cable should be removed |
| Transformers and switchgear | `WSV1_MV_EQUIPMENT_THERMAL` | none | T4 · Class values are engineering judgment | T2 · Reference part value from the NREL/NLR Q1-2025 benchmark crosswalk |  |
| Grounding and lightning protection | `WSV1_GROUNDING_THERMAL` | none | T4 · Class values are engineering judgment | T2 · Reference part value from the NREL/NLR Q1-2025 benchmark crosswalk | *Key assumption:* Low response, not immunity |
| SCADA and communications | `WSV1_SCADA_THERMAL` | none | T4 · Class values are engineering judgment | T2 · Reference part value from the NREL/NLR Q1-2025 benchmark crosswalk |  |
| Civil: fencing, roads, buildings, site prep | `WSV1_CIVIL_DIRECT` | none | T4 · Class values are engineering judgment | T2 · Reference part value from the NREL/NLR Q1-2025 benchmark crosswalk | *Known bias:* Mixed civil row treated as all direct civil (conservative) |

**How to use this curve**

- Damage is a share of: Pre-event direct replacement value of the same part; the plant view uses the named reference profile WILDFIRE_SOLAR_REFERENCE_100MWDC_V1 or complete site part values
- Single event: allowed: per-part damage ratio for one exact class, or the expected ratio over the six-class probabilities
- Scenario dollars: conditional: needs an explicit value profile or complete site part values
- Yearly loss: conditional: computed by the consumer with FSim burn probability in the frequency layer and cap-binding checks passed; curve spread not carried
- Condition: Only exact integer classes 0 to 6; no interpolation or extrapolation
- Condition: Six-class probabilities must each lie in [0, 1] and sum to one
- Condition: Burn probability is not allowed in the damage call
- Condition: Outputs carry screening flags: not field or claims calibrated; FSim class is not local heat flux

**Scope**

- Not covered: Replacement support and fieldwork: no own curve; allocated once at the aggregate direct-and-civil damage ratio (T4 rule)
- Out of scope: Equipment-origin fire and battery storage; Power shutoffs, downtime, business interruption and insurance terms; Post-fire erosion or landslide, environmental remediation and fire-service liability; Soft and non-physical cost (installed capex above physical replacement value)
- Missing mechanisms: Smoke and ash optical losses and module cleaning

**Key sources** (from the cell's source register)

- USDA Forest Service, Spatial datasets of probabilistic wildfire risk components for the US, 3rd ed., RDS-2016-0034-3 (USFS_FSIM_RDS_2023)
- DOE/FEMP, Solar Photovoltaic Hardening for Resilience - Wildfire (DOE_FEMP_PV_WILDFIRE)
- NEMA GD 2-2016, Evaluating Fire- and Heat-Damaged Electrical Equipment (NEMA_GD2_2016)
- FM, Data Sheet 7-106: Ground-Mounted Solar Power, April 2026 (FM_DS_7_106_2026)
- NREL/NLR, Q1-2025 Solar PV System Cost Benchmarks (NREL_NLR_Q1_2025_PV_BENCHMARK)

**Our judgment (T4 items)**

- Damage values per flame-length class for every part are engineering judgment (no class-specific field data)
- Racking, foundations and grounding get a low response, not immunity
- Support cost is allocated in proportion to direct-and-civil damage

**Outside checks**

- Result check, Hazard repo: Financial range check (Hazard repo): industry loss figures for solar wildfire ([link](https://github.com/aamani-ai/Hazard_Modeling/blob/main/docs/data_sources/financial_range_solar_wildfire/profile.md))

**Open items**

- No field or claims calibration; values to be replaced when paired exposure, disposition and cost evidence arrives
- No credit yet for site controls (vegetation, barriers, suppression, de-energisation); kept as metadata
- Reference profile counts all cable as exposed and the mixed civil row as direct civil; site schedules should replace it

<a id="flood-wind"></a>

### Wind farm × Flood

**Live** · model v1.0, docs r1 · `flood_wind` · [curve file](flood_wind/current/flood_wind__model_v1_0__docs_r1__curve_artifact.json) · 2026-10-19: Agent-drafted, from the cell's own tier table and release decision

**Input:** Freshwater flood depth above substation grade (ft), 0 to 10 ft; or water-surface and grade elevations (m) on the same vertical datum

**Method:** Adopted as published. FEMA Hazus-MH 2.1 Table 7.9 whole-substation depth-damage table used exactly as published (0 to 10 ft, damage 0 to 0.15), linear between one-foot points.

| Part | Curves | Variants | Shape | Cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GSU / substation (whole facility) | `FW_HAZUS_2_1_SUBSTATION_SCREENING_PWL` | Hazus substation class ESSL, ESSM or ESSH (same points) | T3 · Hazus 2.1 Table 7.9 points; official but legacy, no claims calibration | T3 · Same Hazus table gives damage as a share of the substation's replacement value; denominator row T3 | *Key assumption:* Whole-substation unit; never charge it together with the GSU component parts |

**How to use this curve**

- Damage is a share of: Full direct replacement value of the same facility-level GSU/substation (not project TIV, not the mixed 72 USD/kW electrical row)
- Single event: conditional: exact Hazus substation class, the Hazus 2.1 Table 7.9 assumption set, freshwater non-contaminated water, depth 0 to 10 ft
- Scenario dollars: conditional: only with an explicit same-substation replacement value and exposure fraction
- Yearly loss: withheld for this partial screening release (consumer-owned)
- Condition: substation_hazus_class must be ESSL, ESSM or ESSH (all three use the same points)
- Condition: Salt, brackish, contaminated or unknown water withholds
- Condition: Depth must be unprotected or internal post-bypass depth; no extra mitigation credit
- Condition: Negative depth rejects, depth above 10 ft withholds, missing depth rejects (never treated as dry)
- Condition: One shared substation is counted once, never repeated by turbine count or across solar and wind
- Condition: The cell gives no covered value share; the substation value must come from the site

**Scope**

- Not covered: GSU parts as separate units: switchgear, main transformer, transformer auxiliaries and controls, protection and SCADA, station service and DC, cable terminations (withheld, not zero); Turbine-base electrical and pad or turbine step-up transformers (withheld); Collection cable joints and terminations (withheld); Turbine foundation (needs a separate scour and erosion pathway) and civil access and drainage (needs a split); Elevated turbine equipment: rotor, nacelle, tower (geometry-screened, not declared zero); Fieldwork and transport support (allocated once after repair scope; no fragility)
- Out of scope: Outage restoration, business interruption, curtailment, revenue and insurance; Soft, sunk and non-physical costs (excluded from the physical base); Other hazards in the same event (tropical-cyclone wind, tornado); one event must not charge the same value twice
- Missing mechanisms: Scour, erosion, saturated-soil support loss, debris impact and wave loading; Flood duration (captured but has no effect on the result)

**Key sources** (from the cell's source register)

- FEMA, Hazus-MH Flood Model Technical Manual 2.1, Table 7.9 (FW-S011)
- FEMA, Hazus 7.0 Flood Technical Manual (2025), electric-power status (FW-S012)
- USACE, HEC-FIA Technical Reference, depth-percent damage relationships (FW-S006)
- NEMA GD 1-2016, Evaluating Water-Damaged Electrical Equipment (FW-S002; historical context)
- NREL, Cost of Wind Energy Review 2024 (FW-S008; value anatomy only)

**Our judgment (T4 items)**

- Only freshwater non-contaminated water gets a number; all other water types withhold
- No extension past 10 ft: deeper water withholds instead of holding the last value
- Missing or incomplete depth is rejected, never read as dry
- Flood duration is recorded but does not change the result
- The whole-substation curve and any future component curves must never be charged together
- Unknown ownership keeps the substation out of the baseline

**Outside checks**

- None yet

**Open items**

- Review of the 2026 NEMA successor guide (CS 70006-2026) is still open
- Current Hazus 7.0 disables electric-power loss functions; the table is legacy and not claims-calibrated
- Component-level GSU curves could replace the whole-substation curve later
- Salt and contaminated water response not modelled

<a id="tropical-cyclone-wind-wind"></a>

### Wind farm × Hurricane wind

**Live** · model v1.2, docs r2 · `tropical_cyclone_wind_wind` · [curve file](tropical_cyclone_wind_wind/current/tropical_cyclone_wind_wind__model_v1_2__docs_r2__curve_artifact.json) · 2026-10-19: Agent-drafted, from the cell's own tier table and decision log

**Next version:** Model v1.3 proposal: same curve, tower value re-based to 276 of 1,623 USD/kW (17.0% of a $162.3M physical TIV, $27.6M covered); not yet released

**Input:** Peak 3-second gust at 10 m (km/h); zero at or below 90, evaluated 108 to 252; for the canonical 5 MW proxy 90 to 108 returns zero and above 252 returns the maximum (both flagged)

**Method:** Adopted as published. Published fitted expected-damage curves for generic steel turbine towers (Wind Energy, 2020) used as published; the 3.3 MW / 100 m curve stands in for the canonical 5 MW turbine, tower value only.

| Part | Curves | Variants | Shape | Cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Turbine tower | `TCWW_JAIMES_1MW_44M_SCREENING`<br>`TCWW_JAIMES_2P5MW_80M_SCREENING`<br>`TCWW_JAIMES_3P3MW_100M_SCREENING`<br>`TCWW_JAIMES_3P3MW_AS_CANONICAL_5MW_TOWER_PROXY_V1` | source archetypes 1 MW / 44 m, 2.5 MW / 80 m, 3.3 MW / 100 m; canonical 5 MW / 100 m tower proxy (3.3 MW parameters unchanged) | T3 · Published fitted curve shape and archetype parameters | T4 · Damage-state cost ratios and the denominator quarantine are T4; the 0.16 tower share is owner-approved (no tier code) | *Key assumption:* The 5 MW turbine uses the 3.3 MW curve unchanged; no capacity scaling |

**How to use this curve**

- Damage is a share of: Tower value of the canonical 5 MW wind farm (0.16 of project TIV); source archetypes use the paper's own turbine/tower cost, which must not be multiplied by CWER values or site TIV
- Single event: conditional: exact turbine archetype and source-assumption IDs; the canonical 5 MW route also needs the tower-proxy policy, asset-profile and value-basis IDs
- Scenario dollars: conditional: only with an explicit tower value and exposure; covered loss capped at 0.16 of project TIV per event
- Yearly loss: conditional: consumer-computed with validated hurricane frequency and intensity, 0.16 occurrence and annual caps, and disclosure that 0.84 is withheld
- Condition: Saffir-Simpson category and NHC one-minute sustained wind are not accepted inputs
- Condition: No averaging-period, height, terrain or hub-height bridge is included
- Condition: A known operating state that differs from the source assumption withholds
- Condition: No 5/3.3 capacity scaling and no rotor or nacelle value binding
- Condition: Covered value is the tower only: 0.16 of canonical project TIV ($22.4M of $140M); the other 0.84 is withheld

**Scope**

- Not covered: Rotor, nacelle, foundation, pad electrical, collection, GSU/substation, control building and SCADA, civil, fieldwork and transport (withheld, not zero)
- Out of scope: Storm surge, flood, scour, debris, rain ingress, lightning and fire; Business interruption
- Missing mechanisms: Blade and other non-tower turbine failure modes (the curve is driven by tower damage states only)

**Key sources** (from the cell's source register)

- Probabilistic risk assessment on wind turbine towers subjected to cyclone-induced wind loads, Wind Energy 23(3), 528-546 (2020) (JAIMES_2020_TC_WIND_TURBINE / TCWW-S005)
- Canonical wind-farm reference profile: 20 x 5 MW, $140M, tower share 0.16 (CONUS_WIND_FARM_REFERENCE_V1)
- Owner scope correction authorizing the tower-only 0.16 binding (OWNER_SCOPE_CORRECTION_2026_08_14; governance, not evidence)
- Hazard hurricane wind-farm EAL review that found the 0.63 value mismatch (HAZARD_HURRICANE_WIND_FARM_EAL_REVIEW_2026_08_14)
- NREL, Cost of Wind Energy Review 2024 (TCWW-S010; comparison only)

**Our judgment (T4 items)**

- No damage at or below 90 km/h is a source assumption, not measured
- Damage-state cost ratios (1 MW 2/43/100%, 2.5 MW 4/48/100%, 3.3 MW 5/50/100%) are the source authors' assumptions
- The source's own cost denominator is ambiguous and is kept quarantined
- All non-tower parts are withheld, not zero

**Outside checks**

- Result check, Hazard repo: Financial range check (Hazard repo): tower-value ceiling for wind-farm hurricane loss (shared lineage; no open industry loss figures found) ([link](https://github.com/aamani-ai/Hazard_Modeling/blob/main/docs/data_sources/financial_range_wind_farm_hurricane/profile.md))

**Open items**

- No target-matched 5 MW evidence
- No separate rotor, blade, nacelle, foundation, electrical, substation, civil or support curves
- Curve spread and damage-state probabilities not carried
- No external financial-range validation of the annual results

<a id="wind-tornado-wind"></a>

### Wind farm × Convective wind

**Live** · model v1.0, docs r4 · `wind_tornado_wind` · [curve file](wind_tornado_wind/current/wind_tornado_wind__model_v1_0__docs_r4__curve_artifact.json) · 2026-10-19: Agent-drafted, from the cell's own tier table and derivation write-up

**Next version:** Model v2.0 proposal (not indexed): separate straight-line and tornado direct-hit pathways with ordered damage states, narrowed to one turbine-equipment assembly on a 1,090 USD/kW (2023) denominator

**Input:** Hub-height 3-second gust (m/s), or 10 m gust with a height bridge, divided by the IEC class 50-year gust (Ve50 = 1.4 x Vref); tornado via an EF-scale gust proxy; no fixed range (extrapolation warns)

**Method:** Built from references. Engineering-fit logistic curves on hub gust over the IEC 50-year gust, built from IEC design speeds, the NIST fragility method and EF4 case evidence; tornado is a curve shift.

| Part | Curves | Variants | Shape | Cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Blade | `WT_BLADE_STRUCT` | straight-line wind or tornado direct hit (D50 shift -0.10); IEC class I, II or III | T4 · Engineering-fit D50 ratio and steepness | T3 · max_DR 1.0 cap T3; the 0.173 value share is not tiered by the cell |  |
| Tower | `WT_TOWER_STRUCT` | straight-line wind or tornado direct hit (D50 shift -0.12); IEC class I, II or III | T4 · Engineering-fit D50 ratio and steepness | T3 · max_DR 1.0 cap T3; the 0.169 value share is not tiered by the cell |  |
| Nacelle | `WT_NACELLE_CONSEQ` | straight-line wind or tornado direct hit (D50 shift -0.10); IEC class I, II or III | T4 · Engineering-fit D50 ratio and steepness | T3 · max_DR 0.85 cap T3; the 0.345 value share is not tiered by the cell | *Key assumption:* Often consequential to blade or tower failure; summing may double count |
| Foundation | `WT_FOUNDATION_OT` | straight-line wind or tornado direct hit (D50 shift -0.08); IEC class I, II or III | T4 · Engineering-fit D50 ratio and steepness | T3 · max_DR 0.65 cap T3; the 0.062 value share is not tiered by the cell |  |
| Power electronics | `WT_POWER_ELEC_ACCEL` | straight-line wind or tornado direct hit (D50 shift -0.05); IEC class I, II or III | T4 · Engineering-fit D50 ratio and steepness | T4 · max_DR 0.3 cap T4; the 0.037 value share is not tiered by the cell | *Opt-in only:* Not in the default structural aggregate (open seam) |

**How to use this curve**

- Damage is a share of: Each part's default share of the physical replaceable base (blade 0.173, tower 0.169, nacelle 0.345, foundation 0.062, power electronics 0.037), times the exposed turbine fraction
- Single event: allowed: failure-unit damage ratio
- Scenario dollars: conditional: needs an explicit value and exposure basis
- Yearly loss: conditional: consumer-computed from sampled frequency and intensity, a coupling model and caps applied inside the simulation; curve spread not carried
- Condition: IEC wind class selects the speed scale (default IEC II); a turbine design speed can override it
- Condition: Hub height is required for 10 m input; the default 1/7 power-law exponent is flagged and a missing bridge fails closed
- Condition: exposed_turbine_fraction is required
- Condition: Tornado uses the same curves with a lower 50% point (D50 shift)
- Condition: Default parts cover 0.749 of the physical base (blade 0.173 + tower 0.169 + nacelle 0.345 + foundation 0.062); power electronics 0.037 only when opted in

**Scope**

- Not covered: SCADA and controls, electrical collection, substation and civil infrastructure (reviewed secondary units, no curve)
- Out of scope: Tropical-cyclone and hurricane wind (separate neighbouring cell)
- Missing mechanisms: Operating, feathered and yaw state are flags only, with no numeric effect

**Key sources** (taken from the cell's write-up)

- IEC 61400-1 design classes and Ve50 = 1.4 x Vref (DTU_IEC_61400_1, ASHES_IEC_EXTREME_EVENTS)
- NIST, Fragility curves, damage matrices and wind-induced loss estimation (NIST_FRAGILITY_METHOD)
- US DOE, How do wind turbines survive severe weather and storms (DOE_SEVERE_WEATHER)
- NOAA/NWS, Enhanced Fujita scale (NOAA_NWS_EF_SCALE)
- NASA Earth Observatory, Greenfield EF4 tornado damage (NASA_GREENFIELD_TORNADO)

**Our judgment (T4 items)**

- The 50% damage points (D50 ratios) for every part are engineering fits
- Curve steepness (k) for every part is an engineering fit for sparse evidence
- Tornado direct-hit shifts of the 50% point (-0.05 to -0.12) are placeholders
- Power electronics maximum damage of 0.3 is a judgment cap

**Outside checks**

- Result check, Hazard repo: Financial range check (Hazard repo): value-envelope ceiling for wind-farm convective wind (shared lineage; no open industry loss figures found) ([link](https://github.com/aamani-ai/Hazard_Modeling/blob/main/docs/data_sources/financial_range_wind_farm_convective_wind/profile.md))

**Open items**

- Blade, tower, nacelle and foundation damage are summed; a damage-state dependency matrix is still needed
- Measured tornado-on-turbine fragility remains sparse
- Candidate v1.1 items not adopted: numeric yaw-error conditioner, tornado shift refinement, IEC class II/III offsets
- Curve spread not carried

**Files:** [write-up](wind_tornado_wind/current/wind_tornado_wind_curve_derivation_dossier_v1_0.md)

<a id="wildfire-wind"></a>

### Wind farm × Wildfire

**Live** · model v1.0, docs r1 · `wildfire_wind` · [curve file](wildfire_wind/current/wildfire_wind__model_v1_0__docs_r1__curve_artifact.json) · 2026-10-19: Agent-drafted, from the cell's own tier table and release decision

**Input:** USFS FSim conditional flame-length class (RDS-2016-0034-3, 270 m), exact integer 1 to 6 (0 = no-event control); a class, not equipment heat flux

**Method:** Built from references. Cell-local Tier-4 screening points per FSim flame-length class, adopted under owner direction; research supports the mechanism and relative ordering, not the numbers.

| Part | Curves | Variants | Shape | Cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pad electrical | `WWV1_PAD_ELECTRICAL_FSIM_T4` | none | T4 · Tier-4 point array per flame-length class | T4 · Same T4 point array sets the damage level as a share of the unit's value; no separate cost table | *Key assumption:* Numbers match a wildfire_solar profile; the cell treats that as an audit comparison only |
| GSU protection, control and DC | `WWV1_GSU_PROTECTION_CONTROL_DC_FSIM_T4` | none | T4 · Tier-4 point array per flame-length class; T3 support for ranking controls above steel-enclosed gear | T4 · Same T4 point array sets the damage level as a share of the unit's value; no separate cost table | *Key assumption:* One shared package per site, counted once |

**How to use this curve**

- Damage is a share of: Direct replacement value of the same named unit (one pad's electrical equipment, or the one shared GSU protection-control-DC package)
- Single event: conditional: exact FSim product ID, exact integer class 1 to 6, and the Tier-4 screening assumption-set ID
- Scenario dollars: conditional: only with an explicit same-unit replacement value and local exposure fraction
- Yearly loss: withheld for this partial screening release
- Condition: screening_assumption_set_id must equal WW_T4_PARTIAL_ELECTRICAL_SCREENING_2026_08_08
- Condition: Non-integer, unknown or out-of-range classes are rejected
- Condition: No full-project TIV, mixed 72 USD/kW row or whole-farm damage ratio
- Condition: The shared GSU package is counted once
- Condition: Covered value share not stated by the cell; the mixed 72 USD/kW electrical row must be split by the site

**Scope**

- Not covered: Turbine fire assembly: blades, nacelle, tower (withheld, not zero); Collection network, GSU main transformer, GSU switchgear and bus, GSU cable terminations (withheld); Control, met-station and O&M buildings; foundation; civil (withheld); Fieldwork and transport support (allocated once after repair scope; no fragility)
- Out of scope: Internal turbine or electrical fire, lightning and maintenance fires; Business interruption, revenue, PSPS and shutdown; Post-fire erosion, flood and landslide; Soft, sunk and non-physical costs
- Missing mechanisms: Firebrand attack and destructive residue or soot (separate deferred pathways); Mitigation or clearance credit and operating state (captured, no numeric effect)

**Key sources** (from the cell's source register)

- USFS, Spatial datasets of probabilistic wildfire risk components for the US (270 m), 3rd ed., RDS-2016-0034-3 (2023) (WW1-S001)
- Assessing wildfire risk to critical infrastructure in central Chile: an electrical substation, Int. J. Wildland Fire (2024) (WW1-S002)
- NEMA GD 2-2016, Evaluating Fire- and Heat-Damaged Electrical Equipment (WW1-S003)
- USFS, Wildfire vulnerability of power transmission and distribution infrastructure (2015) (WW1-S004)
- Owner direction to represent wildfire-wind risk for one or two subsystems (WW1-A001; business decision)

**Our judgment (T4 items)**

- Pad electrical damage points per flame-length class are a Tier-4 screening assumption
- GSU protection-control-DC damage points per flame-length class are a Tier-4 screening assumption
- Non-integer and out-of-range classes are rejected rather than interpolated
- Curve spread is not carried

**Outside checks**

- None yet

**Open items**

- Validated bridge from FSim class to the heat and firebrand attack an asset actually receives
- Inspected repair-or-replace outcomes and same-unit costs
- Exogenous fire separated from internal, lightning and maintenance fires
- No curve yet for the turbine fire assembly or the other GSU parts

<a id="hail-real-estate"></a>

### Real estate × Hail

**Proposal** · model v0.1, docs r1 · `hail_real_estate` · [curve file](hail_real_estate/proposed/hail_real_estate__model_v0_1__docs_r1__curve_artifact.json) · 2026-10-19: Agent-drafted, from the cell's own tier table and decision log

**Input:** Hazard's MESH75 hail diameter (mm), read as the largest hailstone at the building, 0 to 203.2 mm

**Method:** Built from references. Published hail-damage thresholds by roofing material (onset and full failure) turned into a replacement probability, times the roof's share of building cost.

| Part | Curves | Variants | Shape | Cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| House roof (asphalt shingles) | `HRE_RES_ROOF_ASPHALT_SHINGLE_LAMINATED` | none | T3 · Haag field threshold 1.25-2.0 in | T3 · Hazus roofing 3% x 1.25 = 3.75% of building cost | *Key assumption:* Laminated shingles assumed (3-tab: +42% yearly loss in the NRI check) |
| Warehouse roof (standing-seam steel) | `HRE_IND_ROOF_STANDING_SEAM_STEEL` | none | T3 · Haag onset 2.5 in (T3); full at 3.5 in is judgment (T4) | T4 · 12% roof share (judgment) | *Key assumption:* Cosmetic dents not counted |
| Office roof (TPO membrane and insulation) | `HRE_OFF_ROOF_TPO_MEMBRANE_AND_INSULATION` | none | T3 · Haag and IIBEC threshold 1.0-2.0 in | T3 · Hazus roof cover and insulation (1.1% + 0.7%) x 1.25 x 1.20 = 2.7% | *Key assumption:* Mechanically attached membrane assumed (adhered on a cover board: -72% yearly loss) |
| House walls and windows | `HRE_RES_WALLS_WINDOWS_T4` | none | T4 · judgment thresholds for siding and glass | T4 · judgment unit costs | *Opt-in only:* Needs the walls-and-windows acknowledgement code |
| Warehouse windows | `HRE_IND_WINDOWS_T4` | none | T4 · judgment glass threshold | T4 · judgment unit cost | *Opt-in only:* Needs the walls-and-windows acknowledgement code |
| Office windows | `HRE_OFF_WINDOWS_T4` | none | T4 · judgment glass threshold | T4 · judgment unit cost | *Opt-in only:* Needs the walls-and-windows acknowledgement code |

**How to use this curve**

- Damage is a share of: Each part's own replacement value (roof cover; walls and windows); building share = unit damage x the part's share of structure replacement cost
- Single event: conditional: proposal, not in the runtime index; part and building required
- Scenario dollars: withheld until the building value is qualified
- Yearly loss: withheld before promotion (computed by the consumer afterwards)
- Condition: The walls-and-windows unit answers only with the acknowledgement HRE_T4_WALLS_WINDOWS_SCREENING_2026_10_18
- Condition: Above 203.2 mm withholds

**Scope**

- Not covered: Outdoor equipment: AC condenser, rooftop units (whether it sits in the profile value is an open question)
- Out of scope: Contents (declared as a withheld placeholder part); Wind and flooding from the same storm (other cells)
- Missing mechanisms: Rain entering after a roof breach; Cosmetic denting; Wear from repeated small hail

**Key sources** (from the cell's source register)

- Haag Engineering, hail damage threshold sizes for common roofing (HRE-S001)
- Haag Engineering, low-slope roof systems and hail (HRE-S002)
- IIBEC, ice-ball impact resistance of heat-aged TPO membranes (HRE-S005)
- FEMA, Hazus 7.0 Hurricane Technical Manual, building cost ratios (HRE-S006)
- FEMA National Risk Index, Dec 2025 (HRE-S012; check only)

**Our judgment (T4 items)**

- Hazard's MESH75 size read as the hailstone at the building
- Threshold band read as a 5%-95% range
- Warehouse roof share 12% of building cost (range 9-15%)
- Walls and windows thresholds, exposure and costs (no published thresholds)
- Outdoor equipment withheld

**Outside checks**

- Curve check: FEMA National Risk Index: yearly roof loss on Hazard's grid ([link](hail_real_estate/proposed/NRI_CHECK_hail_real_estate__model_v0_1__docs_r1.csv))

**Open items**

- Hazard's MESH75 floor (every severe pixel at least 1.5 in) drives most of the gap to NRI
- Shingle type and office membrane attachment not in the profiles
- Whether outdoor equipment sits in the profile value (for the reviewer)

### Real estate × Flood

**Proposal** · model v0.2, docs r1 · `flood_real_estate` · [curve file](flood_real_estate/proposed/flood_real_estate__model_v0_2__docs_r1__curve_artifact.json) · 2026-10-19: Agent-drafted, from the cell's own tier table and decision log

**Input:** Water depth above the first floor (ft), -4 to 24 ft (retail coastal curve -1 to 10 ft); depth above ground is accepted with the building's floor height

**Method:** Adopted as published. FEMA Hazus depth-damage functions used as published, one per building (house DF 129, warehouse DF 341, office DF 431, each for river and coastal still water); retail keeps Hazus DF 217 for river water and USACE NACCS for coastal surge.

| Part | Curves | Variants | Shape | Cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| House | `FRE_RES_HAZUS_DF129` | water: river or coastal (same curve) | T2 · Hazus DF 129 points | T2 · Hazus loss ratio of replacement value |  |
| Warehouse | `FRE_IND_HAZUS_DF341` | water: river or coastal (same curve) | T2 · Hazus DF 341 points | T2 · Hazus loss ratio of replacement value |  |
| Office | `FRE_OFF_HAZUS_DF431` | water: river or coastal (same curve) | T2 · Hazus DF 431 points | T2 · Hazus loss ratio of replacement value | *Known bias:* Reads about 1.6x the NFIP claims for 3+ storey buildings |
| Retail | `FRE_COM_FRESH_HAZUS_DF217`<br>`FRE_COM_COAST_NACCS_P2`<br>`FRE_COM_COAST_NACCS_P2_MIN`<br>`FRE_COM_COAST_NACCS_P2_MAX` | water: river (Hazus DF 217) / coastal (NACCS, with low and high building-variant bounds) | T2 · Hazus DF 217 and NACCS published points | T2 · source loss ratios of replacement value | *Not a Hazard profile:* Kept from v0.1; not a current Hazard profile |

**How to use this curve**

- Damage is a share of: Structure replacement cost new of the same building (no land, contents or depreciation)
- Single event: conditional: proposal, not in the runtime index; the request must name the building and the water type
- Scenario dollars: withheld until the building value is qualified
- Yearly loss: withheld before promotion (computed by the consumer afterwards)
- Condition: flood_water_type is required; unknown water withholds
- Condition: When Hazard sends depth above the floor it must apply the dry-ground rule itself (depth above ground of 0 or less means no damage)

**Scope**

- Not covered: nothing in the asset's value is left without a curve
- Out of scope: Contents (declared as a withheld placeholder part); Land, site works, business interruption
- Missing mechanisms: Waves and fast-moving water (wave and velocity zones)

**Key sources** (from the cell's source register)

- FEMA, Hazus Flood Model Technical Manual 7.0 (2025), Table 5-2 (FRE-S002)
- FEMA Hazus 6.1 flood damage-function extract (FRE-S010)
- USACE, North Atlantic Coast Comprehensive Study (2015), depth-damage functions (FRE-S004)
- FEMA OpenFEMA NFIP redacted claims, v3 (FRE-S012; check only)
- Hazard reference profiles r1 (FRE-S013)

**Our judgment (T4 items)**

- No value per area set, so scenario dollars stay withheld
- No adjustment for the gap between river and coastal claims (coastal commercial claims run higher)

**Outside checks**

- Curve check: NFIP flood-insurance claims by depth band (about 105,000 claims) ([link](flood_real_estate/proposed/NFIP_CLAIMS_CHECK_flood_real_estate__model_v0_1__docs_r1.md))

**Open items**

- Office curve reads about 1.6 times the claims for 3+ storey buildings (kept as published)
- Wave and velocity zones not modelled
- Contents placeholder: keep or drop (for the reviewer)

**Method:** Adopted as published. FEMA Hazus hurricane building-loss rows used as published (every 5 mph, five terrain classes) for the Hazus building type and wind characteristics matching each building; the 32 Hazus curves used are identical in FEMA's 6.1 extract and SimCenter's independent 5.1 copy.

| Part | Curves | Variants | Shape | Cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| House | `TCRE_RES_HAZUS_WSF1_*` | terrain: open, light suburban, suburban, light trees, trees | T2 · Hazus WSF1 building-loss rows | T2 · Hazus loss ratio of replacement value | *Key assumption:* Older national-default roof connections (code-built reads lower) |
| Warehouse | `TCRE_IND_HAZUS_SPMBL_NEWDECK_*` | terrain x 5 | T2 · Hazus SPMBL building-loss rows (new or average roof deck) | T2 · Hazus loss ratio of replacement value | *Key assumption:* Large overhead doors not represented in Hazus |
| Office | `TCRE_OFF_HAZUS_SECBM_*` | terrain x 5 | T2 · Hazus SECBM building-loss rows (tier as for the other Hazus rows) | T2 · Hazus loss ratio of replacement value |  |
| Retail | `TCRE_COM_HAZUS_SECBL_*` | terrain x 5 | T2 · Hazus SECBL building-loss rows | T2 · Hazus loss ratio of replacement value | *Not a Hazard profile:* Kept from v0.1; not a current Hazard profile |

**How to use this curve**

- Damage is a share of: Structure replacement cost new of the same building
- Single event: conditional: proposal, not in the runtime index; building and terrain class required
- Scenario dollars: withheld until the building value is qualified
- Yearly loss: withheld before promotion (computed by the consumer afterwards)
- Condition: hazus_terrain_class is required (open, light suburban, suburban, light trees, trees); never defaulted and never also applied to the gust
- Condition: Below 50 mph returns 0; above 250 mph withholds

**Scope**

- Not covered: nothing in the asset's value is left without a curve
- Out of scope: Contents (declared as a withheld placeholder part); Land, site works, business interruption; Storm surge and rain flooding (flood cell)

**Key sources** (from the cell's source register)

- FEMA, Hazus 7.0 Hurricane Model Technical Manual (2025) (TCRE-S001)
- FEMA Hazus 6.1 hurricane damage and loss function extract (TCRE-S002)
- NHERI SimCenter, Hazus 5.1 hurricane loss functions, independent copy (TCRE-S003)

### Real estate × Convective wind

**Proposal** · model v0.1, docs r1 · `convective_wind_real_estate` · [curve file](convective_wind_real_estate/proposed/convective_wind_real_estate__model_v0_1__docs_r1__curve_artifact.json) · 2026-10-19: Agent-drafted, from the cell's own tier table and decision log

**Input:** 3-second gust at 10 m (mph), 0 to 255 mph; separate fields for storm wind and tornado (tornado: Hazard's EF band midpoint gust)

**Method:** Built from references. EF tornado-scale damage steps for each building type, each priced on FEMA's Hazus damage-state cost ladder; tornado used directly, storm wind as a transfer starting at 96 mph.

| Part | Curves | Variants | Shape | Cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| House | `CWRE_RES_EF_FR12_STRAIGHT_LINE_ONSET96`<br>`CWRE_RES_EF_FR12_TORNADO` | pathway: storm wind (from 96 mph) / tornado | T3 · EF FR12 damage-step speeds (expert elicitation) | T4 · our placement of each step on the Hazus cost ladder | *Key assumption:* House shifted off foundation priced at 50% (100% would raise 120 mph damage by 16 points) |
| Warehouse | `CWRE_IND_EF_MBS_STRAIGHT_LINE_ONSET96`<br>`CWRE_IND_EF_MBS_TORNADO` | pathway: storm wind (from 96 mph) / tornado | T3 · EF MBS damage-step speeds | T4 · our placement of each step on the Hazus cost ladder |  |
| Office | `CWRE_OFF_EF_LRB_STRAIGHT_LINE_ONSET96`<br>`CWRE_OFF_EF_LRB_TORNADO` | pathway: storm wind (from 96 mph) / tornado | T3 · EF LRB damage-step speeds | T4 · our placement of each step on the Hazus cost ladder |  |

**How to use this curve**

- Damage is a share of: Structure replacement cost new of the same building
- Single event: conditional: proposal, not in the runtime index; pathway and building required
- Scenario dollars: withheld until the building value is qualified
- Yearly loss: withheld before promotion (computed by the consumer afterwards)
- Condition: Each pathway reads only its own gust field; an EF rating is never accepted as a speed
- Condition: Storm-wind damage is zero at or below 96 mph
- Condition: A tornado spawned by a hurricane is priced in one cell only

**Scope**

- Not covered: nothing in the asset's value is left without a curve
- Out of scope: Contents (declared as a withheld placeholder part); Land, site works, business interruption; Hurricane wind (hurricane cell)

**Key sources** (from the cell's source register)

- Texas Tech WSEC, A Recommendation for an Enhanced Fujita Scale, Rev 2 (2006) (CWRE-S001)
- NOAA Storm Prediction Center, EF scale damage indicators FR12, MBS, LRB (CWRE-S002)
- FEMA, Hazus 7.0 Hurricane Technical Manual, damage-state costs and definitions (CWRE-S003)
- FEMA National Risk Index, Dec 2025 (CWRE-S006; check only)

**Our judgment (T4 items)**

- Which FEMA damage level each EF damage step belongs to (incl. house foundation shift = 50%, kept for now)
- Light damage priced at 1%
- EF speed range read as a 90% spread
- Storm wind starts at 96 mph
- Storm wind uses tornado-derived evidence
- EF speeds taken as 10 m open-terrain gusts; no terrain adjustment

**Outside checks**

- Curve check: FEMA National Risk Index: yearly loss on Hazard's grid (storm wind and tornado) ([link](convective_wind_real_estate/proposed/NRI_CHECK_convective_wind_real_estate__model_v0_1__docs_r1.csv))

**Open items**

- Storm-wind yearly loss reads well above the NRI level (largely Hazard's storm frequency)
- Alternative route for the reviewer: reuse the hurricane building curves

**Method:** Built from references. US Forest Service home loss by flame-length class (shrub vegetation) for the house; warehouse 0.8x and office 0.9x from same-fire CAL FIRE inspection ratios.

| Part | Curves | Variants | Shape | Cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| House | `WFRE_RES_WRC_SHRUB` | none (vegetation fixed at shrub) | T3 · Forest Service home response by class | T4 · our reading of the loss figure as rebuild-cost share |  |

| Office | `WFRE_OFF_WRC_SHRUB_X0_9` | none | T3 · house response x 0.9 (CAL FIRE same-fire ratio) | T4 · our reading of the loss figure as rebuild-cost share |  |

**How to use this curve**

- Damage is a share of: Structure replacement cost new of the same building
- Single event: conditional: proposal, not in the runtime index; building and FSim product required

### Substation × Flood

**Live** · model v1.0, docs r1 · `flood_substation` · [curve file](flood_substation/current/flood_substation__model_v1_0__docs_r1__curve_artifact.json) · 2026-10-19: Agent-drafted, from the cell's own tier table, capability, consumer binding and decision log

**Consumer binding inside this cell:** [substation_flood_screening_v1](../contracts/hazard_handoff/substation_flood_screening_v1/binding.json)

**Input:** Water depth above station grade (ft) at the facility point, 0 to 10 ft; sub-peril (pluvial, riverine or coastal) must be stated; deeper or missing depth is withheld

**Method:** Adopted as published. FEMA Hazus-MH 2.1 Table 7.9 whole-substation depth-damage ratios used as published (0 to 15% over 0 to 10 ft), the same table already carried by the flood_wind cell.

| Part | Curves | Variants | Shape | Cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Whole station (fenced assembly) | `FW_HAZUS_2_1_SUBSTATION_SCREENING_PWL` | sub-peril: pluvial, riverine or coastal (same curve); Hazus class ESSL, ESSM or ESSH (same points) | T3 · Hazus Table 7.9 points, linear between them (Coastal use is a T4 transfer) | T4 · Hazus loss ratio (T3) applied to a fenced value whose match to the Hazus denominator is T4 (SUB-A01) | *Reused from:* Same Hazus table as the flood_wind substation assembly (FW_HAZUS_GSU_SUBSTATION_ASSEMBLY)<br>*Key assumption:* Coastal uses the river depth curve with no salt or wave effect (T4) |

**How to use this curve**

- Damage is a share of: Replacement value of the same fenced station, $27,353,236.37 (MISO MTEP24 published table amounts, no extra uplift), applied once
- Single event: conditional: whole-station damage ratio for a stated sub-peril and a depth of 0 to 10 ft; deeper or missing depth returns no value
- Scenario dollars: allowed with the same-station value: damage ratio times $27.35M fenced value, no component terms added
- Yearly loss: conditional: Hazard computes it only after frequency, missing-mass, station cap and tail checks pass; screening composite, not complete risk or portfolio total
- Condition: One canonical 150 x 178 m 345/138 kV station; not an observed asset
- Condition: Depth at facility grade; no equipment-height shift, area multiplier or protection credit
- Condition: Coastal is a T4 depth-only transfer; it does not mean the water is fresh
- Condition: Use the whole assembly once; do not add component curves on top
- Condition: Cap yearly station loss at its replacement value; keep missing probability mass with a tag

**Scope**

- Not covered: nothing in the asset's value is left without a curve
- Out of scope: External access road and project support allowances ($3.06M, outside the fenced value; unmodeled, not zero); Land and anything outside the fence; Movable contents, outage and business interruption
- Missing mechanisms: Salinity and contamination; Waves; Velocity and scour; Debris

**Key sources** (from the cell's source register)

- FEMA, Hazus-MH 2.1 Flood Technical Manual, Table 7.9 (FW-S011)
- flood_wind source register: current Hazus electric-power losses disabled (FW-S012)
- Substation flood consumer binding: canonical station and value (SUB-A01)
- Owner-selected screening scope and Coastal equal-depth transfer (SUB-A02)

**Our judgment (T4 items)**

- One canonical 345/138 kV station and its fenced value stand in for any station (SUB-A01)
- Coastal water uses the same depth curve with no salt or wave adjustment (SUB-A02)
- Civil and site works counted inside the fenced value is an engineering interpretation

**Outside checks**

- None yet

**Open items**

- Equipment-local curves and heights deferred to the component research backlog
- No qualified response above 10 ft or for coastal salt and wave effects
- National completion of Hazard's cloud run still to be verified

<a id="substation-hurricane-screening-v1"></a>

### Substation × Hurricane wind

**Reused** · SUBSTATION_TC_WIND_ASSEMBLY_SCREENING_V1 · `substation_hurricane_screening_v1` · [binding](../contracts/hazard_handoff/substation_hurricane_screening_v1/binding.json) · 2026-10-19: Agent-drafted, from the binding README, binding.json and the source cell's tier table

**Input:** Pressure ratio: (event 3-second gust / ASCE MRI300 reference design gust, 10 m, Exposure C) squared, valid 0 to 2; STORM 10-minute wind converted by (1/0.88) x 1.20; outside the range is unavailable, not clamped

**Method:** Reused from another cell. The canonical solar TC-wind GSU/substation assembly curve is already separate from the solar array, so it is reused for the standalone station without inventing a solar plant (see docs/contracts/hazard_handoff/substation_hurricane_screening_v1/README.md).

| Part | Curves | Variants | Shape | Cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Whole station (fenced assembly) | `TCWS21_GSU_SUBSTATION_SCREENING_T4_ORDERED_STATES` | resistance: lower, central or upper (unweighted) | T4 · Source medians and beta are T4 in the solar cell; the yard transfer is also T4 | T4 · Source state costs 0 / 0.08 / 0.35 / 1 are T4; fenced value membership is T4 | *Reused from:* tropical_cyclone_wind_solar v2.1 docs r2 (TCWS21_GSU_SUBSTATION_SCREENING_T4_ORDERED_STATES)<br>*Key assumption:* Resistance set by a regional ASCE MRI300 design, not observed capacity |

**How to use this curve**

- Damage is a share of: Replacement value of the same fenced station, $27,353,236.37 (MISO MTEP24 published table amounts), applied once
- Single event: conditional: whole-station damage ratio for a pressure ratio of 0 to 2 and an explicit resistance scenario (lower, central or upper)
- Scenario dollars: conditional: same conditions, damage ratio times the $27.35M fenced value; no component losses added
- Yearly loss: conditional: Hazard computes capped yearly metrics after frequency, spatial coupling, value and cap qualification; not a portfolio total
- Condition: Pin the source artifact (tropical_cyclone_wind_solar v2.1 docs r2) and this binding by hash
- Condition: Event and design gusts must share the same duration, height and exposure convention
- Condition: Resistance scenarios are unweighted sensitivities, not probabilities
- Condition: Cap yearly station loss at $27,353,236.37
- Condition: A zero result does not mean the station is immune

**Scope**

- Not covered: nothing in the asset's value is left without a curve
- Out of scope: External access road and project support allowances ($3.06M, outside the fenced value; unmodeled, not zero); Storm surge and rain flooding (Flood entry); Tornado (convective wind binding); Business interruption, revenue and insured interest
- Missing mechanisms: Wind-driven rain; Windborne debris

**Key sources** (taken from the cell's write-up)

- Canonical tropical_cyclone_wind_solar model v2.1 docs r2, curve TCWS21_GSU_SUBSTATION_SCREENING_T4_ORDERED_STATES
- Hazard substation profile (asset_model.json): 345/138 kV AIS, two 336 MVA transformers
- MISO MTEP24 published cost tables (fenced station value)
- ASCE MRI300 parent-cell screening design reference (demand bridge)

**Our judgment (T4 items)**

- GSU-to-transmission-yard assembly transfer
- Source state medians, beta 0.35 and state costs are synthetic choices, not calibrated
- Regional ASCE MRI300 design reference stands in for station capacity
- Civil and site works counted inside the fenced value

**Outside checks**

- None yet

**Open items**

- National delivery is Hazard's next step
- A future component response must replace the overlapping assembly scope and be requalified

### Substation × Convective wind

**Reused** · SUBSTATION_CW_DIRECT_WIND_SCREENING_V1 · `substation_convective_wind_screening_v1` · [binding](../contracts/hazard_handoff/substation_convective_wind_screening_v1/binding.json) · 2026-10-19: Agent-drafted, from the binding README, binding.json and the source cell's tier table

**Input:** Pressure ratio: (event 3-second gust / ASCE MRI300 reference design gust, 10 m, Exposure C) squared, valid 0 to 2; Strong Wind uses ASCE 3-second gusts, Tornado uses the EF-band midpoint gust; outside the range is unavailable, not clamped

**Method:** Reused from another cell. Same station assembly and same direct aerodynamic loading on a squared 3-second gust ratio, so the hurricane GSU/substation curve is reused as a T4 cross-hazard proxy for direct wind only (see docs/contracts/hazard_handoff/substation_convective_wind_screening_v1/README.md).

| Part | Curves | Variants | Shape | Cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Whole station (fenced assembly) | `TCWS21_GSU_SUBSTATION_SCREENING_T4_ORDERED_STATES` | pathway: strong wind or tornado direct loading; resistance: lower, central or upper (unweighted) | T4 · Source medians and beta are T4; the cross-hazard transfer is also T4 | T4 · Source state costs 0 / 0.08 / 0.35 / 1 are T4; fenced value membership is T4 | *Reused from:* tropical_cyclone_wind_solar v2.1 docs r2 (TCWS21_GSU_SUBSTATION_SCREENING_T4_ORDERED_STATES)<br>*Known bias:* Direct wind only; tornado debris and pressure-change damage left out |

**How to use this curve**

- Damage is a share of: Replacement value of the same fenced station, $27,353,236.37 (MISO MTEP24 published table amounts), applied once
- Single event: conditional: whole-station direct-wind damage ratio for a pressure ratio of 0 to 2 and an explicit resistance scenario
- Scenario dollars: conditional: same conditions, damage ratio times the $27.35M fenced value
- Yearly loss: conditional: Hazard supplies frequency, tornado footprint contact, severity and count law, then one station cap; direct-wind screening contribution only
- Condition: Pin the source artifact (tropical_cyclone_wind_solar v2.1 docs r2) and this binding by hash
- Condition: No hurricane duration conversion; inputs are already 3-second gusts
- Condition: Resistance scenarios are unweighted sensitivities, not probabilities
- Condition: Strong Wind and Tornado run as independent yearly streams, then one cap of $27,353,236.37
- Condition: Not a complete tornado loss; unknown event mass kept with tags

**Scope**

- Not covered: nothing in the asset's value is left without a curve
- Out of scope: External access road and project support allowances ($3.06M, outside the fenced value); Business interruption and service interruption; Overlap with Hurricane wind (not deduplicated; a downstream Total decision)
- Missing mechanisms: Tornado-only mechanisms: windborne debris, pressure change, rotation and duration; Cascading electrical failures

**Key sources** (taken from the cell's write-up)

- Canonical tropical_cyclone_wind_solar model v2.1 docs r2, curve TCWS21_GSU_SUBSTATION_SCREENING_T4_ORDERED_STATES
- NIST, design guide for the new tornado load requirements in ASCE 7-22
- NIST, explanation of tornado loading (2024), incl. Joplin substation damage
- NWS Enhanced Fujita scale wind bands
- Substation Hurricane screening binding (station and value qualification)

**Our judgment (T4 items)**

- Hurricane-to-non-hurricane direct-wind transfer
- Tornado EF-midpoint gust used on the pressure axis
- Equivalent-square footprint, uniform value and parallel path overlap for tornado contact
- GSU-to-transmission-yard transfer and fenced civil membership carried from the Hurricane binding

**Outside checks**

- None yet

**Open items**

- A complete tornado response needs the deferred component and pathway research
- Regional Fano factor kept after contact thinning (not an exact derivation)
- Strong Wind and Hurricane overlap left to a downstream Total decision

### Substation × Wildfire

**Reused** · substation_wildfire_electrical_screening_v1 · `substation_wildfire_screening_v1` · [binding](../contracts/hazard_handoff/substation_wildfire_screening_v1/binding.json) · 2026-10-19: Agent-drafted, from the binding README, binding.json and the source cell's tier table

**Input:** FSim fire intensity class at the station reference point, exact integer 1 to 6 (0 = no event); no interpolation or heat-flux conversion

**Method:** Reused from another cell. The canonical solar wildfire transformer/switchgear (MV equipment) response is reused once for the station's transformer and switchgear equipment as a T4 assembly transfer (see docs/contracts/hazard_handoff/substation_wildfire_screening_v1/README.md).

| Part | Curves | Variants | Shape | Cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Electrical equipment (transformers and switchgear) | `WSV1_MV_EQUIPMENT_THERMAL` | none | T4 · Source class ordinates are T4; the MV-to-HV transfer is also T4 | T4 · Source damage ratio is already a share of value (T4); equipment row membership is T4 | *Reused from:* wildfire_solar v1.0 docs r3 (WSV1_MV_EQUIPMENT_THERMAL)<br>*Key assumption:* FSim class is landscape severity, not local heat at the equipment |

**How to use this curve**

- Damage is a share of: Bound electrical equipment value of the station, $13,025,357 (eight equipment rows); % of TIV divides by the full fenced value $27,353,236.37
- Single event: conditional: equipment damage ratio for an exact FSim class at the facility point
- Scenario dollars: conditional: damage ratio times $13,025,357; remaining fenced value withheld
- Yearly loss: conditional: Hazard computes it after frequency, class, value, cap and spatial-aggregation proof; capped at $13,025,357
- Condition: Pin the source artifact (wildfire_solar v1.0 docs r3) and this binding by hash
- Condition: Burn probability and class probability stay separate, in Hazard
- Condition: No extra contact, perimeter, gravel, firebreak, firewall or enclosure credit
- Condition: Apply the one response once to the declared assembly; no child losses on top
- Condition: Withheld station value is a response gap, not immunity

**Scope**

- Not covered: Rest of the fenced station ($14,327,879.37, 52.38%): bus supports, dead-ends, oil containment and firewall, relay panels, control house, station battery, SCADA, station service, control cable, conduit and trench, site work, drainage and lightning shielding
- Out of scope: External access road and project support allowances ($3.06M, outside the fenced value); Business interruption, revenue and insurance terms

**Key sources** (taken from the cell's write-up)

- Canonical wildfire_solar model v1.0 docs r3, WSV1_MV_EQUIPMENT_THERMAL (ordinate table and value linkage)
- USFS FSim RDS-2016-0034-3 (native fire class and burn probability)
- Hazard substation profile (asset_model.json): 345/138 kV AIS, two 336 MVA transformers
- MISO MTEP24 published cost tables (equipment value rows)

**Our judgment (T4 items)**

- MV-to-HV electrical assembly transfer
- Source class ordinates are engineering judgment, not measured failure rates
- Instrument and protection equipment counted inside the modeled electrical assembly

**Outside checks**

- None yet
