<a id="flood-bess"></a>

### Battery storage × Flood

**Live** · model v1.0, docs r1 · `flood_bess` · [curve file](flood_bess/current/curve_artifact.json) · 2026-10-19: Agent-drafted, from the cell's own tier table, capability and decision log

**Input:** Water depth above local grade (m), finite and 0 or more; water type must be stated as fresh or saline; the PCS freshwater curve reads depth above the assumed 0.30 m entry (0 to 2 m knots, flat at full replacement beyond 0.6 m)

**Method:** Built from references. Conservative entry policy (replace once water is above 0.30 m) for battery enclosures, plus the Flood Solar inverter curve reused for the separate PCS; unit values from market cost shares of the fixed Hazard reference budget.

| Part | Curves | Variants | Shape | Cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Battery enclosure (active hardware) | `BESS_ACTIVE_CONTACT_STATE` | water: fresh or saline (same rule: full replacement once depth is strictly above 0.30 m) | T4 · 0.30 m entry step is an owner-approved policy, not a fragility (BF-Q01) | T4 · Full replacement on entry is policy; the $901,380 unit value split is T3 | *Key assumption:* Water assumed to enter at 0.30 m above grade<br>*Known bias:* Conservative policy, not a calibrated mean |
| Separate PCS | `BESS_PCS_INUNDATION_PROXY`<br>`BESS_PCS_SALINE_CONTACT_STATE` | water: fresh (inverter curve on depth above 0.30 m entry) / saline (full replacement above 0.30 m) | T3 · Flood Solar inverter knots (T3); the entry offset, deep plateau and saline step are T4 | T3 · Same-unit value $520,000 from market cost shares (T3) | *Reused from:* flood_solar v1.0 docs r4 (FS_INV inverter curve) |

**How to use this curve**

- Damage is a share of: Hardware replacement value of the same physical unit, fixed real-2024 dollars: $901,380 active hardware per enclosure (80), $520,000 per PCS (20); $82.5M covered of $109.8M total
- Single event: allowed: per-unit damage ratio for a stated depth and a stated water type (fresh or saline); unknown water or missing depth is withheld
- Scenario dollars: allowed with the same-unit value and exposure stated; covered hardware only, never scaled to the whole plant
- Yearly loss: conditional: Hazard computes it only if frequency, shared event, per-unit cap and missing-data checks pass; partial-property result only, complete-plant figures withheld
- Condition: Pin the exact v1.0 artifact, value and profile; one value per unique physical unit
- Condition: Use Hazard's existing inland annual-maximum or Coastal event-rate clock; no invented category probabilities
- Condition: Interpolate depth before the response; apply the 0.30 m entry once
- Condition: All units share one event; the plant stays fixed within the year
- Condition: Cap each unit's yearly cost at its replacement value; no repair within the year
- Condition: Keep missing source and response probability; do not turn unmodeled value into zero

**Scope**

- Not covered: Enclosure racks and fire suppression ($11.89M); Electrical balance including unit transformers and cables ($13.2M); Civil works ($1.6M); Unallocated fieldwork ($0.6M)
- Out of scope: Collector station and export line; Autonomous internal failures (not caused by the flood); Business interruption
- Missing mechanisms: Wave impact; Scour; Debris

**Key sources** (from the cell's source register)

- Hazard BESS reference r1: profile, layout and 2024 budget (BF-S01)
- NEMA GD 1-2016, Evaluating Water-Damaged Electrical Equipment (BF-S02)
- Flood Solar model v1.0 docs r4 canonical artifact (BF-S06)
- SMA MV Power Station with Sunny Central Storage system manual (BF-S12)
- NREL PVSCM 2024 Q1 cost model, ESS rows (BF-S13)

**Our judgment (T4 items)**

- Water enters the enclosure and PCS at 0.30 m above grade (owner-approved policy, not measured)
- Any entry means full replacement of the enclosure's active hardware (BF-Q01)
- Saline water above 0.30 m means full replacement of enclosure and PCS hardware (BF-Q02)
- Freshwater PCS damage stays at full replacement past the last source point (no deep-water data)

**Outside checks**

- None yet

**Open items**

- Coastal first SLOSH depth bin (0-1 ft) straddles the 0.30 m entry; upper-bin sensitivity kept for the spatial pilot
- $27.29M of the plant value has no flood response yet
- Matched service evidence, more mechanisms, restoration and size/duration scaling are future work

**Input:** Pressure ratio: (event 3-second gust / declared reference gust) squared, dimensionless, valid 0 to 2; outside the range is withheld, not clamped

**Method:** Built from references. Solar TC-wind ordered damage-state curves reused as a T4 hypothesis, with BESS enclosure state costs from a related NREL cost split and full replacement at major damage.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Integrated battery enclosure | `BESS_ENCLOSURE_TC_REPLACE_MAJOR_V0_1`<br>`BESS_ENCLOSURE_TC_REPAIR_SENSITIVITY_V0_1` | response: approved replacement / repair sensitivity; resistance: lower, central or upper (unweighted) | T4 · State medians and beta transferred from the solar TC-wind curve, not fitted (BW-P02) | T4 · State costs 0 / 0.14 / 1 / 1 (repair sensitivity 0.19 at major) from policy and a related cost split (BW-P03 to P06) | *Key assumption:* Major damage means replacing the whole enclosure (BW-Q01) |

- Yearly loss: conditional: Hazard computes it only after frequency, shared-event coupling, per-unit cap and annual-distribution checks pass; partial-property result only, complete-plant figures withheld

- Condition: Cap each unit's yearly cost at its value; no repair within the year
- Condition: Keep unknown source and domain probability; the $15.4M unbound property is not zero

**Scope**

- Not covered: Unit MV and shared electrical ($13.2M); Civil works ($1.6M); Fieldwork ($0.6M)
